# Meet the woman behind chart-topping AI artist Xania Monet (CBS News)

By Gayle King. Published November 5, 2025.

## Key findings
- **Telisha "Nikki" Jones** (31, Mississippi) created Xania Monet: "Xania is an extension of me, so I look at her as a real person."
- Jones is **not a singer**; the lyrics are "100% me," from poems based on real life (losing her dad at 8 inspired "How Was I Supposed to Know?").
- Process: puts lyrics into an AI music-generator (Suno), adds prompts — "slow tempo R&B, **female soulful vocals**, light guitar and heavy drums" — then clicks create.
- Multi-million-dollar exclusive deal with **Hallwood Media**; backlash from **Kehlani** ("nobody will be able to justify AI to me," "I don't respect it").
- **Digital blackface concern:** Jones responded, "That's what I'm here to let them know, **I'm Telisha. I'm a part of your culture; I'm a Black woman; I'm a creator; I'm an entrepreneur; I created Xania**."
- Hallwood A&R head Danny Jacobson: AI is "breaking down barriers around age, image, and access."

## Assessment
- `authoritative: yes` — CBS News (top-tier), primary interview with the creator.
- Establishes: Jones is a **Black woman**; the persona is a **female soulful-voiced** R&B artist; the "digital blackface" framing was raised and answered; the visual/voice are AI-constructed while lyrics are Jones's own.
